### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1caee8cbd363e06692317cabd3c5746ba0b976be` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37799ebb962a5853fb7e1f1d188adb5a71dff7be` — the merge of head `ce2f6fefa12d4fb2a846af796fdf71d03b2b672d` into base `1caee8cbd363e06692317cabd3c5746ba0b976be`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37799ebb962a5853fb7e1f1d188adb5a71dff7be && git checkout 37799ebb962a5853fb7e1f1d188adb5a71dff7be
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1caee8cbd363e06692317cabd3c5746ba0b976be ce2f6fefa12d4fb2a846af796fdf71d03b2b672d && git checkout -B drift-repro 1caee8cbd363e06692317cabd3c5746ba0b976be && git merge --no-ff ce2f6fefa12d4fb2a846af796fdf71d03b2b672d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1caee8cbd363e06692317cabd3c5746ba0b976be
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1caee8cbd363e06692317cabd3c5746ba0b976be` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 full · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `c1bbebce97214da54499af216d3e97d71d39cb84` · card #35137 (`Part of #35137`) · read 2026-11-18T11:29Z

Net diff against merge base `55020c331b`: 9 files, +488 / -6. Not governed. Security-touching.

### Against the card

- **`Part of` is right.**
  - This PR is the framework half: the result member, the note, both doors, the served text and the card's three pins.
  - Under the card's bound and the default object-schema masking, the done-when persona is not reachable. The ask-data skill line and the scenario round are not in this PR either.
  - The bound question is with the maintainer. Merging this PR must leave the card open.
- **The bound is held, and held in one place.** A field is named only when the caller's own served schema shows it and the security service's readable answer for that caller leaves it out. Both answers are asked as the caller, and nothing is derived from rows.
  - `withheldFieldNames` skips any candidate the served set does not contain, even one the call asked for by name.
  - The ablation that deletes that one line turns the two "never named" pins red (tool layer and stdio), and restores clean.
  - The real-security-layer case pins the other direction: for a caller served the whole schema, exactly the denied field is named, so no schema field the read path keeps is reported as withheld.
- **The card's pins are present.** A withheld field is named. A field hidden from the schema is not named anywhere in the serialized result. A readable field with an empty value is not named. Only asked fields are named when `fields` is given. Nothing withheld gives a byte-identical answer.
- **`aggregate_records`.** The card asks for it only "if the door does not already refuse it". The body records a probe on the real security layer: a withheld measure or group key is already refused with a permission error. Leaving that door unchanged is within scope.
- **File surface.** All 9 files are inside claim 6974815741's surface. The claim allowed a read of the security plugin, and no file there changes. The existing caller-scoped readable answer is used.

### Read at the head

- **Tool layer (`mcp-http-tools.ts`).**
  - The new bridge member is optional. A missing member, an `undefined` answer and a throw all name nothing, and the read never fails because of the probe.
  - Members are added only when the list is non-empty.
  - On `query_records` the members sit beside the existing delegation notice, and a test covers both together. `get_record` gets the members after its not-found path, so an unreadable id still answers as before.
  - The note is one constant and names no field and no value.
- **HTTP bridge (`runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`).** It reads the served schema through `readObjectForCaller`, the projection `describe_object` uses, and the readable answer from this request's security service with this request's execution context, the same context the reads use. If there is no security service, no served object or no readable answer, it answers `undefined`.
- **Stdio bridge.** It reads through `servedView` (the object-schema mask view) and the principal `resolvePrincipal` gives, the same two the stdio reads use. The same `undefined` exits apply.
- **Exports.** `McpFieldVisibility` is exported from `@objectstack/mcp` beside `McpDataBridge`. The two bridge-member classification tripwires register the new member.

### Declarations, CI, merge

- **Changeset, read sentence by sentence.** `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime` are both `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: two new result members, one new optional bridge member and a new exported type, and no reply loses a key. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. Each sentence matches the code: names only, asked fields only when `fields` is given, the two-answer rule, no change without the member or the service, and `aggregate_records` unchanged.
- **Published docs.** `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` lists the record tools but no result members, so no published sentence becomes false. The served text gains its one line in both tool descriptions.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 53 in total, all completed, none failed (37 `success`, 16 `skipped`).
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `910306b632`.

### Nits (none blocks)

- The changeset names the exact capabilities that put a caller in the whole-schema posture. They are published ADR-0106 terms, but the seat should weigh them under the card's disclosure rule before landing.
- The follow-up skill bullet is quoted in dev report 6976419490 but has no card yet. The card stays open for it, the scenario and the ruling. Filing the `domain:skills` card now would make that carrier visible.
- Each `query_records` and `get_record` call now makes two more framework reads (the served schema and the readable answer), even for callers with nothing withheld. This is correct, but worth a look if MCP read latency is ever measured.

### Not mine, still owed before landing

- **The maintainer's ruling** on the bound (a decision thread). The PR is built on option A and does not land before the ruling.
- **Contract review** at this head (running), which checks the bound against `references/lanes/security.md`.
- Sequencing with area o1-D's #35145 branch, which shares four files and has one textual conflict in `mcp-http-tools.ts`. Whichever lands second merges main.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c1bbebce97214da54499af216d3e97d71d39cb84`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #35137 (body, triage 6971739882 / 6974332801 / 6974554954, claim 6974815741, dev report 6976419490), PR #35179 (body, 9-file list, net diff against merge base `55020c331b`, every PR comment), the 53 check-runs on this head (37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure: every derived gate family green, Test Core 10/10, Type Check debt ledger, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards), and, at this head, `plugin-security` (`getReadableFields`, `computeReadableFields`, the field mask and its fold), ADR-0106 D1/D4/D8 as the bridges implement them, and `describe_object` on both doors. Judged as option A of the open question (keep the bound).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set / public surface — `McpDataBridge.fieldVisibilityOf?` (new OPTIONAL member) and the exported type `McpFieldVisibility`: right.** Optional with the `diagnoseDelegation` degradation contract: absent member, `undefined` answer or throw adds nothing and never fails the read. The only two implementers in-repo are the HTTP bridge (`buildMcpBridge`) and the stdio bridge; no wrapper re-lists bridge members, so no door silently drops it. Both bridge-member classification tripwires register it as reading no row. Every other implementer keeps compiling and behaving as before.
- **Result surface — `withheldFields` + `withheldFieldsNote` on `query_records` and `get_record`: right.** Names only, never a value; the note and the two description sentences are constants that name no field. Absent when the list is empty, so an unrestricted caller's answer is byte-identical (pinned against a bridge with no member). Not added on a not-found `get_record` (the 404 is thrown first) nor on any error path.
- **Withheld half = the security service's own caller-scoped answer: right.** `getReadableFields`, asked with the same execution context the read itself runs under (HTTP: the request's `ec`, the one `callData` receives; stdio: the same `resolvePrincipal()` context the engine read gets). It is the documented complement of the read mask's delete set (partial-mask columns count readable, the computed-field fold and the delegator intersection are included), so a withheld field is named from the framework's answer, never from comparing rows.
- **Served half = `describe_object`'s mask for THIS caller: right on masking and on D4/D8** — the HTTP bridge reads `readObjectForCaller` (the `/meta` object door's masker and projection, resolved once per request, same as `describe_object`); stdio reads `servedView`, the same caller view `describe_object`'s localized view wraps (translation renames nothing). The D4-exempt and D8-off cases are pinned on stdio and, on the real security layer, on HTTP. **Not exact in every case — see S1.**
- **Bound on asked fields: right.** With `fields` given, only asked names are candidates and each must be in `served`; an asked name outside the caller's schema is never named anywhere in the serialized result (pinned on the tool layer and on real stdio; ablation of the intersection line turns both pins red). These two tools take no expand/nested projection, so no related-object path is opened.
- **`aggregate_records` unchanged: right.** The card scoped it "if the door does not already refuse it"; the security layer's query guard already refuses an unreadable field as a group or measure, and that refusal is pinned in `plugin-security`'s own suite. The dev's MCP-door probe was uncommitted (N1).
- **Descriptions:** one sentence each on `query_records` and `get_record` — the card's "served text gains one line": right.

S1 (should-fix) — the served-schema half is not computed exactly as `describe_object` serves it in every case, so the card's bound is not held structurally on both doors; a possible security observation went to the seat privately. The fix is local to the two `fieldVisibilityOf` implementations (or one shared derivation), with the existing "served equals describe_object's field names" pin extended to the case where they can differ.

N1 (nit) — the `aggregate_records` "already refused" premise rests on an uncommitted probe at the MCP door; a one-case pin there would keep the reason the tool gains no member from drifting.

N2 (nit) — on `get_record` the two members are merged into the record object itself, beside its field keys (no collision: field machine names are snake_case by the spec regex). A client that echoes a fetched record back into a write carries two non-field keys; `query_records` keeps them on the wrapper. A design choice the card allows, stated here so it is a choice.

N3 (nit) — `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` § The security model lists the surfaces that name fields to a caller; the new member is consistent with it but not listed. Docs-drift is advisory and the skill line is already carried on the card.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/35137-mcp-withheld-fields.md`: `@objectstack/mcp` patch, `@objectstack/runtime` patch. Right: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no authorable key, value or type changes; this is a result member and an optional bridge member), so the level follows the kind and is `patch`. Both published packages the diff moves are named; no third package publishes from this diff.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body: right — a new optional result member and note on two tools, a new optional bridge member and a new exported type, nothing taken away. Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions[0] (does the done-when member persona stand under default schema masking — A keep the bound / B widen / C drop the persona): **escalated, not ruled here.** The PR is built on A, says `Part of #35137`, and the seat's comment holds landing until the maintainer's ruling is recorded on the card; that hold is the right state and is part of this verdict.
- Dev flag: two gate families NOT MEASURED locally (dual-build CJS load, type-check debt): answered by the head's check-runs — Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check · debt ledger and Build Core are success.
- Dev flag: textual overlap with the area o1-D branch for #35145 (no PR yet) in the shared MCP tool file: answered by the claim's serial constraint (whoever lands second merges main and re-runs overlap-check); nothing owed on this head.
- Dev flag: the ask-data skill line and the example-app scenario stay on the card (no governed path in this diff): answered; the card stays open through `Part of`.
- Dev flag: `security_findings: withheld`: the seat's to read; this record adds S1's private note beside it.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The new probe is one schema projection and one readable-fields answer per tool call, never per row or per field, and no ids are materialised and no join is done in the app. The probe runs after `diagnoseDelegation` rather than beside it — a latency nit at most, not a push-down question.

I read the delta only, from `c1bbebce97` (my ACCEPT 6977289014) to this head: one commit, 4 files, +135 / -42. The code is right. What blocks is CI.

### Must fix

- **M1: `Test Core (9/10)` is red** (job 134820624120). The stdio CONTROL case at `src/query-records-withheld-fields.test.ts:285` ("nothing withheld, or no security service…") expects `{ object, records, total: 1 }`. On the merge ref it gets `{ object, records, hasMore: false }`.
  - Main has since changed the stdio `query` answer to the `hasMore` page shape and dropped `total` (CI tests the PR merged onto main).
  - This is a real conflict with main, not a flake. The PR's own runs were on its stale base `55020c331b`, which is why they were green.
  - Fix: merge main and pin the control answer as main now serves it. The pin should still prove what it is there for: no `withheldFields` and no note, and the readable answer asked as the principal. Then re-run the package suite on the merged tree.

### The delta, read

- **The served list now comes from `describe_object`'s own answer.** Each door builds that answer in one function: `describeForCaller` on HTTP, `describeForPrincipal` on stdio. `describe_object` and `fieldVisibilityOf` both call it, and `describedFieldNames` reads the names off it.
  - On HTTP the extraction moves the old `describeObject` body unchanged: `readServedObject`, then `servedToCaller`, then `inCallerLocale`, then `describeServedObject`. The stdio extraction is unchanged too.
  - The candidate set can only shrink. A column the served definition carries but `describe_object` does not list (the search companion is pinned on both doors) is never a candidate, so the bound gets tighter, never looser.
  - The two ablations restore the round-1 derivation, and each turns its new pin red.
- **Ruled persona (ruling A, 6977609191).** The bound is unchanged. A whole-schema caller and a masking-off member are told, both pinned. A plain member under default masking is never told, pinned on both doors.
- **`Fixes #35137`.** The body names the remaining halves' carriers: #35191 for the skill line and #35113 for the scenario question.

### Should fix before landing (card hygiene, not this diff)

- **S1.** The question #35113 carries for this card (comment 6971648229) is still written for "a member", the persona ruling A makes unreachable under default masking. Left as written, that round reports a permanent loss, or invites a widening the ruling refused. Add a line on #35113, citing 6977609191, that moves the question to the ruled persona (a whole-schema caller, or a masking-off deployment). Then `Fixes` hands over a question that can pass.

### Not mine, still owed

- A delta from me on the merged head (M1 only).
- The contract review delta at that head.
- Sequencing with #35199 (o1-D), which conflicts in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`. Whichever lands second merges main.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ce2f6fefa12d4fb2a846af796fdf71d03b2b672d`
Local-runs: none

Delta from `c1bbebce97` (contract review 6977363432) to this head. Read: the ruling 6977609191 on #35137, dev reports 6979373052 and 6982233531, L1-b delta 6979759939, head note 6982265326, the PR body at this head, the round-2 commit `380c35a8641`, the re-pin commit `69216b02fde`, the two main merges (`0eaa53f500d`, `ce2f6fefa12`, the second carrying #35199), the PR's net diff against the new merge base `1caee8cbd36` compared file by file with the round-1 net diff, carriers #35191 and #35113 with the persona line 6979780844, and the 57 check-runs on this head (39 success, 18 skipped, 0 failure; Test Core 10/10, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, and Check Changeset and the PR-body guards re-run green after the body edit).

### ① Derived judgments

S1: closed. Both doors now take the served list from `describe_object`'s own answer, so the two lists are equal by construction, not because two derivations happen to agree. On HTTP, `describeObject` is the same function `fieldVisibilityOf` calls (`describeForCaller`). On stdio, `describeObject` returns `describeForPrincipal`, which `fieldVisibilityOf` also calls. Both read names off that answer with `describedFieldNames`. The extracted bodies are the old `describe_object` bodies unchanged: on HTTP the served object, the caller's mask, the caller's locale, then the describe projection; on stdio the localized caller view with its declaration, then the same projection. So `describe_object` serves exactly what it served before. Pinned where the two lists can differ: the real-engine runtime pin is extended, and a stdio twin is added. Each of the two ablations restores the round-1 derivation and turns its own pin red. The candidate set can only have shrunk. The private note went to the seat.

- **Persona pinning against ruling A (6977609191): matches.** The bound is unchanged. A D4-exempt caller is told, pinned on stdio and on HTTP's real security layer. A masking-off (D8) member is told, pinned on stdio, with a new runtime pin on HTTP. A plain member under default masking is never told, even when asking for the field by name, pinned on both doors. Ruling A asks for exactly this split and nothing wider.
- **The merges keep both `latestPer` and `withheldFields` on every path: right.** Compared with round 1, the PR's net diff of the shared tool file differs only in where the description sentence is attached: it now follows the `latestPer` sentences instead of the person-field sentence. The handler hunk is byte-identical. At this head, the `latestPer` branch and the probed-page branch both build `result` through `servedQueryPage`, and `withWithheldFields` runs once on that result before the delegation notice. `get_record`'s line is unchanged.
